title: How Buddhism spread: hearth, diffusion and landscape

parts.label: A
parts.demand: Give the information asked for: a word or short phrase can earn the point, with no reasons needed.
parts.prompt: Identify the world region where Buddhism has its hearth.

rubric.point: Names northeastern South Asia (northern India and southern Nepal, the Ganges plain) as the hearth.
accept: northeastern India
the Ganges River plain
South Asia
northern India and southern Nepal
Bodh Gaya or Lumbini area

parts.sample: Buddhism's hearth is in South Asia, in the Ganges River plain of what is now northeastern India and southern Nepal.

parts.label: B
parts.demand: Give the relevant characteristics: what it is like, where and how much. A name alone earns nothing.
parts.prompt: Describe one difference between how a universalizing religion, such as Buddhism, and an ethnic religion usually spread.

rubric.point: Describes a difference: universalizing religions seek followers from any group and spread by expansion and relocation, while ethnic religions stay mostly near the hearth or spread by relocation.
accept: seeks converts anywhere vs tied to one people
spreads by expansion and relocation vs mostly relocation
followers far from hearth vs near hearth

parts.sample: A universalizing religion such as Buddhism welcomes followers from any people and spreads widely by both expansion and relocation, while an ethnic religion such as Hinduism is tied to one people and mostly stays near its hearth, spreading mainly when followers migrate.

parts.label: C
parts.demand: Say how or why, with every link of the chain: a cause, then because or so, then its effect, tied to the place or data asked about.
parts.prompt: Explain how hierarchical diffusion helped Buddhism spread from its hearth.

rubric.point: Explains a top-down spread with its link: a ruler or elite adopted Buddhism, so it spread to subjects or other lands.
accept: Emperor Ashoka adopted Buddhism and sent monks abroad
rulers in Korea or Japan adopted it first and others followed

parts.sample: In the 200s BCE, the emperor Ashoka adopted Buddhism and sent monks to other lands, including Sri Lanka, so the religion spread from a powerful ruler down to the people he governed and outward to places his monks reached.

parts.label: D
parts.demand: Say how or why, with every link of the chain: a cause, then because or so, then its effect, tied to the place or data asked about.
parts.prompt: Explain how trade routes helped Buddhism spread to East Asia.

rubric.point: Explains that merchants and monks traveling trade routes (such as the Silk Roads) carried Buddhism to new places, with the link stated.
accept: Silk Roads carried monks and merchants into Central Asia and China
sea trade carried it to Southeast Asia

parts.sample: Merchants and monks traveling the Silk Roads carried Buddhist teachings and texts from South Asia through Central Asia into China, because each market town where they stopped brought the religion into contact with new people, so it spread along the route and later on to Korea and Japan.

parts.label: E
parts.demand: Say how or why, with every link of the chain: a cause, then because or so, then its effect, tied to the place or data asked about.
parts.prompt: Explain how chain migration can lead to a cluster of Buddhist temples in one city in the United States.

rubric.point: Explains that early migrants settled in one place and relatives followed, so the community grew there and built temples to serve it (relocation diffusion).
accept: Cambodian refugees in Long Beach, California, and relatives who followed
migrants from Thailand, Viet Nam, Laos or Sri Lanka settling near family

parts.sample: In Long Beach, California, Cambodian refugees settled from the late 1970s on, and relatives later followed them to the same city through chain migration, so a large Buddhist community formed in one area and built temples to serve it.

parts.label: F
parts.demand: Give the relevant characteristics: what it is like, where and how much. A name alone earns nothing.
parts.prompt: Describe one way Buddhism marks the cultural landscape.

rubric.point: Describes a visible feature, such as a stupa, pagoda, temple or monastery, with more than a name.
accept: stupas or pagodas
temples with tiered roofs
statues of the Buddha
monasteries

parts.sample: Buddhists build stupas and pagodas, tall towers that hold relics, such as the gold-covered Shwedagon Pagoda in Yangon, Myanmar, which rises above the city and draws pilgrims.

parts.label: G
parts.demand: State the degree first (to a high, moderate or low degree), then explain why with evidence.
parts.prompt: Explain the degree to which a world map showing the main religion of each country can show the spread of Buddhism to cities in the United States.

rubric.point: States a degree, then explains it with scale: a national-scale world map shows only each country's main religion, so local clusters of Buddhists in US cities do not appear.
accept: to a small or limited degree, with the scale reason
national data hide local clusters

parts.sample: To a small degree: a world map at the national scale colors the United States by its main religion, Christianity, so the Buddhist temples clustered in Long Beach, California, do not appear, and local-scale data, such as a map of places of worship by neighborhood, would be needed to show them.
